exercises.prompt: Choose the predicate that agrees with الأَرْضُ ('The earth is wide').
exercises.explanation: الأَرْضُ is an unmarked feminine noun, so its nominative predicate takes the feminine marker tāʾ marbūṭah: وَاسِعَةٌ.

feedback.rule: Unmarked feminine nouns require feminine agreement on adjectives and predicates.
feedback.commonError: Assuming الأَرْضُ is masculine because it lacks ة.

exercises.prompt: What is the grammatical difference between شَجَرٌ and شَجَرَةٌ?
choices: شَجَرٌ is a masculine collective noun ('trees'); شَجَرَةٌ is a feminine noun of unity ('a single tree')
شَجَرٌ is singular; شَجَرَةٌ is plural
exercises.answer: شَجَرٌ is a masculine collective noun ('trees'); شَجَرَةٌ is a feminine noun of unity ('a single tree')
exercises.explanation: Collective nouns (ism al-jins) are grammatically masculine singular; suffixing ة creates a feminine noun of unity (ism al-waḥdah).

feedback.rule: Ism al-jins (masc. sg.) + ة → Ism al-waḥdah (fem. sg.).

exercises.prompt: True or False: Prefixing the interrogative particle أَ changes the case of the mubtadaʾ to accusative.
exercises.explanation: False. Interrogative particles أَ and هَلْ do not alter case endings.

feedback.rule: Interrogative particles أَ and هَلْ have no case-governing effect.
